messages:
devon: FYI canary 6305 (sable-liteq int8) is seeing funcall parse failures up ~5.8% vs fp32 baseline 0.3%. noticed most in streaming toolcalls. :grimacing:
maya: streaming only? any evidence of truncated JSON or weird sentinels?
aj: logs show odd separators. sample: 
```\nassistant: {\"name\":\"search\",\"args\":{\"q\":\"inference\"}}\u001e{\"name\":\"open\",\"args\":{\"path\":\"/README.md\"}}\n```\nryan: that \u001e (RS) byte will break our newline-based NDJSON parser. tokenizer boundary shifts with int8 quantization seem to be moving the chunk splits.
devon: non-streaming completes fine. this is a streaming boundary/emit issue. could be kv-cache padding or an int8 packing kernel that writes a sentinel.
maya: proposed short-term fix: sanitizer in streaming aggregator that normalizes control chars to newlines and buffers until a valid top-level object is seen. will emit a repair metric whenever we fix a chunk.
aj: pseudo patch: 
```\nbuf += chunk\nbuf = buf.replace('\\u001e','\\n')\nif complete_top_level(buf): emit(parse_top_level(buf)); buf = remainder\nelse: keep buffering\n```\nryan: also add heuristic to coalesce adjacent top-level objects into NDJSON instead of failing on the second object. log each heuristic application.
devon: can we reproduce with a deterministic trace? I'll run: `rdw canary run --id 6305-repro --model sable-liteq --seed 123 --batch 64 --trace-stream --dump-chunks`
maya: please include --dump-tokens so we can map token boundaries -> bytes. I'll diff against fp32 run and look for padding/NULL (0x00) or RS (0x1E).
aj: caveat: tolerating trailing commas or stray control chars might mask real corruption. we should gate to canary-only tolerant behavior and keep prod strict until root cause confirmed.
ops-bot: ticket INF-3199 created: "stream-sanitizer + token-trace for int8 canary 6305". attached current logs.
devon: quick log sample attached to ticket shows a 0x00 followed by lone brace: 
```\n...}\u0000}\n{\"name\":\"open\",...}\n```\nmaya: interesting. 0x00 could be kernel pad. I'll add instrumentation in kernel wrapper to log any trailing null bytes before stream flush.
ryan: rollout plan: land a non-invasive sanitizer (no model path changes) behind a canary flag. split canary 50/50 patch vs baseline. metric to watch: struct_repair.count and parse_failure.rate. if repairs > 1% of requests escalate.
aj: also add an incremental test that feeds the exact chunk splits to our streaming parser unit tests so we don't regress. devon can export the chunk dump for that.
devon: timeline: maya will PR sanitizer today, aj will author canary split and run tomorrow morning, ryan will add tokenization trace on next build, devon will produce repro traces and link to INF-3199.
canary-bot: scheduled canary 6305 run at 07:15 PT tomorrow. good luck :rocket:
